question: What is the main use of emergency equipment in the ward?

options.A: To restore and keep up vital signs during emergencies
options.B: To do daily checks for stable patients
options.C: To replace physical checks by doctors
options.D: To lower hospital bills for long admissions

explanation: Resuscitative devices are designed to step in during sudden, life-threatening events to support failing body systems. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why must nurses know how to use emergency tools quickly?

options.A: Routine schedules need daily staff rotation
options.B: Doctors expect nurses to build new medical gear
options.C: Delays with unfamiliar tools can harm the patient
options.D: Hospital boards test nurses on tool prices

explanation: During emergencies, acting fast is vital because delays directly affect whether a patient survives and recovers. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h1)

question: Which airway tool is best for a semi-conscious patient who still has a gag reflex?
explanation: The nasopharyngeal airway is tolerated better by patients who are not fully unconscious because it does not trigger the gag reflex as easily as oral devices. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h2)

question: How do you know a bag-valve-mask is successfully helping a patient breathe?

options.A: The oxygen tank fills up fast
options.B: Both sides of the chest rise and fall when you squeeze
options.C: The pressure valve makes a constant whistling sound
options.D: The unconscious patient wakes up immediately

explanation: Seeing both sides of the chest move up and down shows that air is entering the lungs instead of just the stomach. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h2)

question: Which heart rhythm needs a defibrillation shock during resuscitation?
explanation: Ventricular fibrillation is a shockable cardiac arrest rhythm where the heart quivers instead of pumping blood properly. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h3)

question: Before discharging a manual defibrillator to give a shock, what safety step must you take first?

options.A: Disconnect all IV infusion pumps from the wall
options.B: Turn the oxygen flow rate to maximum
options.C: Make sure everyone is completely clear of the patient and bed
options.D: Write down the exact time in the nursing notes

explanation: Moving everyone away stops anyone from getting an accidental electrical shock during the high-energy discharge. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h3)

question: How often should nursing staff check emergency crash carts?

options.A: Once a month by the maintenance team
options.D: At the start of every shift

explanation: Checking the cart at the start of each shift ensures all items are present and working before an emergency happens. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h4)

question: What is the main reason for using tamper-evident seals on crash carts?

options.A: To show quickly if any items have been used or removed
options.B: To keep dust out of the drawers
options.D: To lock the wheels during patient transfers

explanation: A broken or missing seal instantly tells the incoming shift that the cart was opened and needs checking and restocking. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h4)

question: What should you do immediately if the electric suction machine fails during an airway emergency?

options.A: Unplug the cord and check the main fuse
options.B: Switch right away to a manual backup suction device
options.C: Wait for the engineer to come from home
options.D: Stop clearing the airway and start chest compressions

explanation: Using manual backup gear ensures patient care keeps going without dangerous delays caused by broken equipment. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h5)

question: What is a common cause of failure in an emergency suction machine?

options.B: The room temperature is too low
options.C: The room thermostat is set wrong
options.D: A loose canister lid or disconnected tubing

explanation: Air leaks from loose seals or disconnected hoses stop the machine from building up the suction pressure needed. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h5)
